title: Making Programs Dynamic

content.title: Reusing variables
content.summary: Change a variable once and the whole program updates automatically.
content.body:
Once you create a variable, you can reuse it anywhere later in the program.

Change the variable once at the top and the whole program updates automatically.

content.title: Building messages from pieces
content.summary: Use + to combine variables and text into one message.
content.body: You can use `+` to join variables and text together into one message.
content.note: Python puts the pieces together in order — variable, then the text you added.

content.title: Python is literal
content.summary: Python only prints exactly what you give it.
content.body:
Python will not add spaces automatically.

If you want a space between words, you have to include it yourself — inside the quotes.
content.codeBlock:
print(name + "entered")    # ❌ Kaientered
print(name + " entered")   # ✅ Kai entered

content.title: Errors are part of programming
content.summary: If Python shows a red error, that's normal — just check the line it mentions.
content.body:
When you run your code, you might see a red error message — that's normal. Python is trying to help you find a mistake.

Most beginner errors are tiny: a missing quote, a missing parenthesis, or a typo. Just check the line Python mentioned.

bonusSteps.editorPrompt: Build a short adventure scene using variables

progressiveHints:
# Try changing the value inside the quotes
name = "Kai"
print(name)

# Use + to combine a variable with text
name = "Kai"

print(name + " entered the castle.")

name = "Kai"
place = "the castle"

print(name + " entered " + place + ".")

name = "Kai"
place = "the castle"
item = "golden key"

print(name + " entered " + place + ".")
print(name + " found a " + item + ".")
